notes_for_us: Survival has no lobby shape, and every round-based genre needs one. The prompt describes the lobby in more detail than any single match map — NPCs, shop, inventory, missions, ranking, training area, queue portal — and it came out as a segment with a null shape.

The task objective is the structural core of asymmetric horror (it is what paces the round and distributes the survivors), and it lives in Simulation's trigger-task. Survival's own table has no objective row at all, only threat, cover and exit.

Almost everything the prompt asks for that is not a map — 15 mechanics entries plus a Luau code request — is correctly out of scope, and the record makes that visible. But 'write all the code in Luau, organised in ModuleScripts' is not a constraint over the *build* in the sense the field means; I filed it there because there is nowhere else.

notes_for_us: The enriched expansion commits to 'occasional dead ends', which is exactly what Survival's genre notes call a hard failure for a chase map ('a single cornered corridor makes a chase game unfair'). A downstream expansion can contradict a genre rule and nothing in the handoff would catch it.

The whole visual identity of the Backrooms — yellow wallpaper, buzzing fluorescents, damp carpet — has no option and rides in theme plus one free-text image entry. Interior surface finish is not expressible as a pick in any genre.

Two questions competed for the same slot: the term question about 'entertes' and the endless-or-exit shape question. Step 5 puts term questions in an exceptional category and step 4 makes the endless question a shape one, so both were justified, but on a 7-word prompt asking two is most of what the user wrote.
